profiles.meeting_scenario: An internal troubleshooting meeting at a company that has integrated a Bayesian patch-prioritization module into its Java CI repair assistant for backend services. Over the past two weeks, the pilot rollout was expected to reduce the number of patch validations needed for recurring test failures, but the operations dashboard shows little improvement and some jobs are taking longer. The meeting agenda is to compare what each side is seeing, identify the most likely reason the ranking gains are not appearing in practice, and agree on a short-term fix or validation plan before expanding the rollout. The expected outcome is a shared action plan for reproducing the issue and narrowing whether the problem lies in patch ranking, trace inputs, or evaluation setup.

members.name: Priya Raman
members.expertise: Automated debugging, fault localization, Bayesian ranking models, Java repair pipelines
members.background: Priya leads the applied-research effort that adapted a Bayesian framework for patch prioritization into the company's internal debugging tooling, and previously completed a PhD focused on automated program repair.
members.private_state: She wants to protect the credibility of the new Bayesian module and suspects the disappointing results are due to integration differences rather than the ranking logic itself; she is also concerned that if the pilot is judged too early, the research-backed rollout will be paused.
hidden_assumptions: When people discuss a 'candidate patch,' they mean a unique, compilable patch that has already passed the pipeline's normalization and deduplication filters.
The production pipeline is already supplying the same kind of value evidence used during internal experiments: failing-test traces plus a small set of confirming passing-test traces.
When colleagues mention 'the replay set' or 'the benchmark,' they are referring to the curated 47-bug Java incident corpus stored in the research S3 bucket.
If the ranking is 'working,' that means developers need to validate fewer patches before reaching the first semantically correct fix, even if total CI wall-clock changes only modestly.

members.name: Lucas Meyer
members.role: Senior Platform Engineer, CI & Developer Productivity
members.expertise: Build orchestration, test infrastructure, observability, rollout operations for developer tools
members.background: Lucas owns the integration of debugging and repair services into the company's CI platform and previously worked on large-scale build systems for Java microservices.
members.private_state: He wants to keep CI latency stable and avoid any extra tracing overhead, and he suspects the new ranking stage is not helping enough to justify its complexity in the live pipeline.
hidden_assumptions: A 'candidate patch' is every template instantiation emitted by the generator, because those all consume queueing, compilation, or scheduler resources before the final shortlist is known.
The pipeline's existing value collector only captures failing-test rerun values in production, since passing-test trace capture was disabled months ago for performance reasons.
When someone says 'the replay set' or 'the benchmark,' they mean the 19 recent internally reproduced CI incidents used by platform engineering for rollout checks.
A ranking is only 'working' if it lowers end-to-end time to a green build or materially reduces executor utilization on real CI jobs.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as a candidate patch
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both discuss reducing the number of 'candidate patches' that need validation.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Priya means normalized, deduplicated, compilable patches that are actually rankable by the Bayesian module.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Lucas means all generated patch instances entering the pipeline, including near-duplicates and patches that fail compile checks.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both meanings are standard within their subteams, and in a troubleshooting discussion 'candidate patch' sounds precise enough that neither expects ambiguity.

misalignment_points.topic: Which value traces are already available
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to using 'the value traces we already collect' to score patches.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Priya assumes the scorer receives the richer trace bundle used in experiments: failing-test values plus a small number of passing-test traces for contrast.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Lucas assumes this refers to the current production collector, which only keeps failing-test rerun values after a prior latency optimization.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: There really is an existing trace pipeline, so the phrase 'already collect' feels shared and uncontroversial; the missing detail is an old operational change Priya does not realize matters here.

misalignment_points.topic: What dataset they are comparing against
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say they checked performance on 'the replay set' and 'the benchmark from last week.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Priya is thinking of the research team's 47-bug curated Java corpus that is rerun nightly in an offline harness.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Lucas is thinking of the platform team's 19 recent reproduced CI incidents executed in staging during rollout verification.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Each team has a routinely used replay set, both were actively run last week, and the label 'the replay set' is common shorthand that normally goes unquestioned.

misalignment_points.topic: What it means for the ranking to be working
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree they need to confirm whether the ranking is 'working' before changing the rollout.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Priya means the ranking should move the first correct patch closer to the top so fewer patch validations are needed before a valid fix is found.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Lucas means the pipeline should produce a faster green CI outcome with lower executor time in live jobs.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase 'working' is a natural summary term in troubleshooting, and both criteria usually correlate enough that neither sees a reason to spell out the exact threshold.

turns.inner_thought: The Bayesian module did exactly what it was supposed to do in the research runs: after normalization and deduplication, it pushed the semantically correct, compilable patches much closer to the top. If the rollout dashboard looks flat, I doubt the ranking logic suddenly stopped working. More likely the live integration is feeding different evidence or evaluating too early. I need to keep this focused on validation count among candidate patches, not let the whole pilot get judged on wall-clock alone before we verify the setup.
